findings.description: Fastify onRequest fires before body parsing, so a signature over a body-hash cannot be computed in an onRequest hook without raw-body handling; codex+copilot flagged this would force consuming the stream or omitting the body hash (weakening the gate).
findings.resolution: Architecture, Risk Areas, US-003, and Implementation Strategy step 3 now require the body-dependent verification to run at preValidation/preHandler (or capture raw body); the hook is split accordingly.
findings.suggestedFix: Split the verifier: signature-meta at onRequest, body-hash check at preValidation/preHandler.

findings.description: Route-coverage completeness anchor and the hostile-client AC enumerated only api.ts:104-117 routes, missing GET / (api.ts:66) and GET /health (enableMonitoring, runs SELECT 1). A hostile-client test built from that list would pass while / and /health stay unauthenticated.
findings.resolution: Hostile-client AC + Risk Areas now enumerate / and /health, anchor completeness on the live Fastify route table (incl. enableMonitoring), and require an explicit default-empty public-path allowlist.
findings.suggestedFix: Add / and /health to the AC enumeration; anchor on the live route table.

findings.description: The codex submodule is uninitialized in fresh plan worktrees; codex paths under codex/external/... do not resolve, so US-008 is not implementable as written without a submodule-init preflight.
findings.resolution: US-001 preflight and the US-008 PREREQ now require `git submodule update --init --recursive` and re-verification of codex paths before editing.
findings.suggestedFix: Add submodule init + path verification as an explicit prereq.

findings.description: Enrollment/revocation lacked a server API shape (no list/revoke routes or their auth rule) and the QR/PIN enrollment gate was underspecified on the daemon side (no mint/display/expire mechanism), making the 'revoke causes fail-closed' AC non-actionable.
findings.resolution: US-002 now defines LAN-gated device-list/revoke server routes + the known-device pin store, and the daemon-side QR/PIN mint/display/expire mechanism (concrete happy-cli command/startup-output/control route with expiry + rate-limit); US-005 implements the mint.
findings.suggestedFix: Define device-list/revoke routes + their LAN auth, and the daemon QR/PIN mint lifecycle.

findings.description: LAN cannot be represented by the current tunnel schemas: packages/happy-cli/src/tunnel/types.ts and packages/happy-wire/src/tunnel/types.ts require Dev-Tunnels-shaped fields (tunnelId/tunnelName/tags/owner) that LAN lacks; left as an open question while US-006 depends on the wire shape.
findings.resolution: US-002 now introduces a discriminated transport: 'dev-tunnels' | 'lan' variant (or optional Dev-Tunnels-only fields) in BOTH packages; the Open Question is marked RESOLVED and not deferrable.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a discriminated transport variant to both tunnel type modules.

findings.description: No concrete daemon-side opt-in source: run.ts:210-211 always constructs DevTunnelsDaemonProvider; a Codex Rust Feature flag cannot by itself change Node daemon startup before /remote on runs.
findings.resolution: Architecture + US-005 now define a happy-cli daemon-side opt-in (env/config/CLI, e.g. HAPPY_LAN_TRANSPORT) read before dualListenerBinding(), explicitly distinct from the codex Feature gate layer.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a persisted/env/CLI daemon opt-in distinct from the codex Feature flag.

findings.description: US-005 depends on more than 'server contract frozen' — it needs the daemon opt-in/config contract (advertised URL shape, auth mode, host bind, machine.json migration) designed before server/app parallelization.
findings.resolution: US-002 (cluster-server, phase 2) now explicitly owns the cross-cutting daemon opt-in + transport contract; cluster-cli and cluster-app (phase 3) depend on cluster-server, so the contract is frozen before parallelization.
findings.suggestedFix: Move the daemon opt-in/transport contract into the phase-2 server-contract story.

findings.description: 'A blessed device completes a remote session from the BOOX over Wi-Fi' is not autonomously verifiable unless the plan defines a non-device integration test or marks the BOOX run as manual evidence.
findings.resolution: AC now requires an automated in-process/loopback blessed-client integration test (the autonomously-verifiable form) and records the physical BOOX run as manual evidence, not a CI gate.
findings.suggestedFix: Add an automated loopback integration test; mark BOOX as manual evidence.

findings.description: The security-model/AGENTS amendments (US-009) are scheduled last, but the code stories relax a protected bind/auth invariant earlier; the reviewed sign-off should land alongside the server-contract change.
findings.resolution: US-003 now records the reviewed relaxed-bind sign-off alongside the gate change; US-009 retains the full docs write-up. AC clarifies the split.
findings.suggestedFix: Record the sign-off with the server-contract story; keep docs polish last.

findings.description: CORS/socket allowedHeaders (api.ts:61-64, socket.ts:105) hard-code X-Tunnel-Authorization/X-Loopback-Capability/X-Happy-Client/Content-Type; new LAN signature headers will fail web/desktop preflight unless added.
findings.resolution: Architecture, Risk Areas, US-003, and US-004 now require adding the LAN header to CORS/socket allowedHeaders and a test pinning it.
findings.suggestedFix: Add the LAN proof header to both allowedHeaders lists.

findings.description: Reusing agentComms/peerAuth.ts directly from happy-cli is the wrong package boundary; happy-server already has @noble/ed25519, @noble/hashes, privacy-kit, tweetnacl, so a small canonical signer/verifier should be extracted/duplicated in the right package rather than coupling happy-server to CLI internals.
findings.resolution: Architecture, In Scope, and US-002 now specify the verifier lives in happy-server (or shared happy-wire) reusing the peerAuth PATTERN via happy-server's own deps, NOT importing happy-cli.
findings.suggestedFix: Own the canonical signer/verifier in happy-server (or happy-wire).

findings.description: US-004 should include CORS/header and raw-body tests before app work starts, so the app does not implement headers/canonicalization the server cannot receive or verify.
findings.resolution: US-004 now explicitly includes CORS-allowed-header and raw-body/preValidation canonicalization tests as part of the decisive acceptance gate before cluster-app.
findings.suggestedFix: Add CORS + raw-body canonicalization tests to US-004.

findings.description: 'Dev Tunnels remains byte-for-byte unchanged' is too vague; pin to observable behavior.
findings.resolution: AC now pins it to: default provider DevTunnelsDaemonProvider, default bind 127.0.0.1, existing pairing/socket/dual-listener tests pass unchanged.
findings.suggestedFix: Pin to default provider/bind + unchanged existing tests.

findings.description: Signature canonicalization AC was not specific enough (exact headers, canonical path/query, timestamp skew, nonce lifetime, socket handshake canonical form, replay failure expectations).
findings.resolution: A dedicated AC now pins the full canonical form, and US-002 owns specifying it with automated expired/replayed/forged tests.
findings.suggestedFix: Specify the full canonical signature form + replay/skew tests.

findings.description: With an empty public-path allowlist the verifier also fail-closes /health; enableMonitoring installs its own onRequest hook (enableMonitoring.ts:8), so the plan should state the LAN hook's ordering relative to it and explicitly decide /health's disposition.
findings.resolution: Architecture and Risk Areas now state the LAN hook fires on every route incl. /health, with stated ordering relative to the enableMonitoring hook and an explicit allowlist decision.

findings.description: 'Formal sign-off' is not a self-contained verification step; specify the sign-off artifact/approver.
findings.resolution: AC now names the sign-off artifact = the docs/security-model.md §Operator Identity Gate amendment + explicit operator approval of the relaxed-bind decision.
findings.suggestedFix: Name the sign-off artifact and approver.

findings.description: The codex WS-transport invariant was cited as packages/happy-cli/AGENTS.md:288 but the sentence sits ~2 lines earlier; cosmetic.
findings.resolution: Citation changed to the section name (## Codex Transport Security Model, ~lines 282-288).
findings.suggestedFix: Cite the section name rather than a single line.
